sanskrit: evaṃ tava prapaśyāmi śreyo bhṛgukulodvaha āgacchato hi te vipra bhaven mṛtyur asaṃśayam
english: Thus, O scion of the line of Bhṛgu, I see what is best for you; for were you to come to me, brahmin, your death would be certain.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tadā rājñā kṣamaṃ buddhimatā hitam samanujñāpya rājānam ahalyāṃ prati jagmivān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the wise king with words fit and salutary, he took leave of the monarch and set out toward Ahalyā.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā kuṇḍale divye gurupatnyāḥ priyaṃkaraḥ javena mahatā prāyād gautamasyāśramaṃ prati
english: Having taken the divine earrings, that doer of kindnesses for his teacher's wife sped with great swiftness toward the hermitage of Gautama.

sanskrit: yathā tayo rakṣaṇaṃ ca madayantyābhibhāṣitam tathā te kuṇḍale baddhvā tathā kṛṣṇājine 'nayat
english: As Madayantī had instructed concerning their safekeeping, so he bound the two earrings and carried them wrapped in a black antelope skin.

sanskrit: sa kasmiṃś cit kṣudhāviṣṭaḥ phalabhārasamanvitam bilvaṃ dadarśa kasmiṃś cid āruroha kṣudhānvitaḥ
english: At one point, overtaken by hunger, he saw a bilva tree laden with a burden of fruit, and, driven by hunger, he climbed it.

sanskrit: śākhāsv āsajya tasyaiva kṛṣṇājinam ariṃdama yasmiṃs te kuṇḍale baddhe tadā dvijavareṇa vai
english: He hung upon its branches that very black antelope skin, O subduer of foes, in which the two earrings had been bound by the best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: viśīrṇabandhane tasmin gate kṛṣṇājine mahīm apaśyad bhujagaḥ kaś cit te tatra maṇikuṇḍale
english: When its binding came loose and the black antelope skin fell to the ground, a certain serpent there caught sight of those jeweled earrings.

sanskrit: airāvatakulotpannaḥ śīghro bhūtvā tadā sa vai vidaśyāsyena valmīkaṃ viveśātha sa kuṇḍale
english: Sprung from the lineage of Airāvata, that swift serpent then seized the earrings in its mouth and entered into an anthill.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇe tu dṛṣṭvā sa kuṇḍale bhujagena ha papāta vṛkṣāt sodvego duḥkhāt paramakopanaḥ
english: Seeing the earrings being carried off by the serpent, distraught and grieving, in extreme wrath he fell down from the tree.

sanskrit: sa daṇḍakāṣṭham ādāya valmīkam akhanat tadā krodhāmarṣābhitaptāṅgas tato vai dvijapuṃgavaḥ
english: Then that bull among the twice-born, his limbs inflamed with anger and indignation, took up a wooden staff and began to dig open the anthill.

sanskrit: tasya vegam asahyaṃ tam asahantī vasuṃdharā daṇḍakāṣṭhābhinunnāṅgī cacāla bhṛśam āturā
english: The Earth, unable to bear his unbearable force, her body battered by the wooden staff, trembled violently and was sorely afflicted.

sanskrit: tataḥ khanata evātha viprarṣer dharaṇītalam nāgalokasya panthānaṃ kartukāmasya niścayāt
english: And so the seer among brahmins kept digging at the floor of the earth, resolved in his determination to carve a path to the world of the serpents.

sanskrit: rathena hariyuktena taṃ deśam upajagmivān vajrapāṇir mahātejā dadarśa ca dvijottamam
english: Then the wielder of the thunderbolt, of mighty splendor, came to that place in his chariot yoked with bays and beheld the best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: sa tu taṃ brāhmaṇo bhūtvā tasya duḥkhena duḥkhitaḥ uttaṅkam abravīt tāta naitac chakyaṃ tvayeti vai
english: Taking on the form of a brahmin, and grieved by his grief, he said to Uttaṅka: 'My son, this cannot be accomplished by you.'

sanskrit: ito hi nāgaloko vai yojanāni sahasraśaḥ na daṇḍakāṣṭhasādhyaṃ ca manye kāryam idaṃ tava
english: 'For the world of the serpents lies thousands of leagues from here; I do not think this task of yours can be achieved with a wooden staff.'

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca nāgaloke yadi brahman na śakye kuṇḍale mayā prāptuṃ prāṇān vimokṣyāmi paśyatas te dvijottama
english: Uttaṅka said: O brahmin, if the earrings cannot be recovered by me from the world of the serpents, I shall give up my life before your very eyes, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: yadā sa nāśakat tasya niścayaṃ kartum anyathā vajrapāṇis tadā daṇḍaṃ vajrāstreṇa yuyoja ha
english: When the wielder of the thunderbolt could not turn his resolve otherwise, he then charged the staff with the power of his thunderbolt weapon.

sanskrit: tato vajraprahārais tair dāryamāṇā vasuṃdharā nāgalokasya panthānam akaroj janamejaya
english: Then the Earth, rent open by those thunderbolt strokes, made a passage to the world of the serpents, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: sa tena mārgeṇa tadā nāgalokaṃ viveśa ha dadarśa nāgalokaṃ ca yojanāni sahasraśaḥ
english: By that road he then entered the world of the serpents, and he beheld that world stretching thousands of leagues.

sanskrit: prākāranicayair divyair maṇimuktābhyalaṃkṛtaiḥ upapannaṃ mahābhāga śātakumbhamayais tathā
english: It was furnished, O fortunate one, with heaps of divine ramparts adorned with gems and pearls and fashioned of pure gold.

sanskrit: vāpīḥ sphaṭikasopānā nadīś ca vimalodakāḥ dadarśa vṛkṣāṃś ca bahūn nānādvijagaṇāyutān
english: He saw pools with crystal stairways, rivers of limpid water, and many trees thronged with flocks of various birds.

sanskrit: tasya lokasya ca dvāraṃ dadarśa sa bhṛgūdvahaḥ pañcayojanavistāram āyataṃ śatayojanam
english: And that perpetuator of the line of Bhṛgu beheld the gateway of that world, five leagues broad and a hundred leagues in length.

sanskrit: nāgalokam uttaṅkas tu prekṣya dīno 'bhavat tadā nirāśaś cābhavat tāta kuṇḍalāharaṇe punaḥ
english: But Uttaṅka, gazing upon the world of the serpents, grew downcast, and once more, my son, he despaired of recovering the earrings.

sanskrit: tatra provāca turagas taṃ kṛṣṇaśvetavāladhiḥ tāmrāsyanetraḥ kauravya prajvalann iva tejasā
english: There a horse, black with a white tail, copper of mouth and eye, blazing as it were with radiance, spoke to him, O Kaurava.

sanskrit: dhamasvāpānam etan me tatas tvaṃ vipra lalpsyase airāvatasuteneha tavānīte hi kuṇḍale
english: 'Blow into this vent of mine, brahmin, and then you shall obtain them; for here the son of Airāvata has carried off your earrings.'

sanskrit: mā jugupsāṃ kṛthāḥ putra tvam atrārthe kathaṃ cana tvayaitad dhi samācīrṇaṃ gautamasyāśrame tadā
english: 'Feel no revulsion in this matter, my son, by any means; for this very thing you yourself performed once in the hermitage of Gautama.'

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca kathaṃ bhavantaṃ jānīyām upādhyāyāśramaṃ prati yan mayā cīrṇapūrvaṃ ca śrotum icchāmi tad dhy aham
english: Uttaṅka said: How should I know you, in connection with my preceptor's hermitage? And what I did there before, that I wish to hear.

sanskrit: aśva uvāca guror guruṃ māṃ jānīhi jvalitaṃ jātavedasam tvayā hy ahaṃ sadā vatsa guror arthe 'bhipūjitaḥ
english: The horse said: Know me to be the teacher of your teacher, the blazing Fire, the knower of all that is born; for I, my child, was ever honored by you for your teacher's sake.

sanskrit: satataṃ pūjito vipra śucinā bhṛgunandana tasmāc chreyo vidhāsyāmi tavaivaṃ kuru mā ciram
english: Always was I worshipped, brahmin, by you in purity, O joy of the Bhṛgus; therefore I shall do what is best for you. Do as I say, and tarry not.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tathākārṣīd uttaṅkaś citrabhānunā ghṛtārciḥ prītimāṃś cāpi prajajvāla didhakṣayā
english: Thus addressed by the Fire of varied splendor, Uttaṅka did accordingly; and the Fire, whose flame is fed with ghee, well pleased, blazed up with the will to consume.

sanskrit: tato 'sya romakūpebhyo dhmāyamānasya bhārata ghanaḥ prādurabhūd dhūmo nāgalokabhayāvahaḥ
english: Then from the pores of his body, as he was being blown upon, O Bhārata, there arose a dense smoke that struck terror into the world of the serpents.

sanskrit: tena dhūmena sahasā vardhamānena bhārata nāgaloke mahārāja na prajñāyata kiṃ cana
english: By that smoke, swelling all at once, O Bhārata, in the world of the serpents, great king, nothing whatsoever could be made out.

sanskrit: hāhākṛtam abhūt sarvam airāvataniveśanam vāsukipramukhānāṃ ca nāgānāṃ janamejaya
english: All the dwelling of Airāvata was filled with cries of dismay, as were the abodes of the serpents led by Vāsuki, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: na prakāśanta veśmāni dhūmaruddhāni bhārata nīhārasaṃvṛtānīva vanāni girayas tathā
english: Choked with smoke, the mansions shone no more, O Bhārata, like forests and mountains shrouded in mist.

sanskrit: te dhūmaraktanayanā vahnitejobhitāpitāḥ ājagmur niścayaṃ jñātuṃ bhārgavasyātitejasaḥ
english: Their eyes reddened by the smoke, scorched by the heat of the fire, they came to learn the purpose of the Bhārgava of surpassing splendor.

sanskrit: śrutvā ca niścayaṃ tasya maharṣes tigmatejasaḥ saṃbhrāntamanasaḥ sarve pūjāṃ cakrur yathāvidhi
english: And having heard the resolve of that great seer of fierce splendor, all of them, their minds thrown into confusion, paid him honor according to the rite.

sanskrit: sarve prāñjalayo nāgā vṛddhabālapurogamāḥ śirobhiḥ praṇipatyocuḥ prasīda bhagavann iti
english: All the serpents, with joined palms, the aged and the young foremost among them, bowed their heads and said: 'Be gracious, O blessed one.'

sanskrit: prasādya brāhmaṇaṃ te tu pādyam arghyaṃ nivedya ca prāyacchan kuṇḍale divye pannagāḥ paramārcite
english: Having appeased the brahmin and offered him water for his feet and the honor-offering, those serpents presented to that most worshipful one the two divine earrings.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpūjito nāgais tatrottaṅkaḥ pratāpavān agniṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā jagāma gurusadma tat
english: Then, honored by the serpents, the mighty Uttaṅka there circled the Fire to the right and set out for that house of his teacher.

sanskrit: sa gatvā tvarito rājan gautamasya niveśanam prāyacchat kuṇḍale divye gurupatnyai tadānagha
english: Going in haste, O king, to the dwelling of Gautama, he then presented the two divine earrings to his teacher's wife, O sinless one.

sanskrit: evaṃ mahātmanā tena trīṃl lokāñ janamejaya parikramyāhṛte divye tatas te maṇikuṇḍale
english: Thus by that great soul, O Janamejaya, after he had traversed the three worlds, were those divine jeweled earrings brought back.

sanskrit: evaṃprabhāvaḥ sa munir uttaṅko bharatarṣabha pareṇa tapasā yukto yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: Of such power was that sage Uttaṅka, O bull of the Bharatas, endowed with supreme austerity, about whom you question me.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca uttaṅkāya varaṃ dattvā govindo dvijasattama ata ūrdhvaṃ mahābāhuḥ kiṃ cakāra mahāyaśāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: After granting the boon to Uttaṅka, O best of the twice-born, what did the mighty-armed Govinda of great renown do thereafter?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dattvā varam uttaṅkāya prāyāt sātyakinā saha dvārakām eva govindaḥ śīghravegair mahāhayaiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having granted the boon to Uttaṅka, Govinda set out together with Sātyaki for Dvārakā itself, drawn by great, swift-paced horses.

sanskrit: sarāṃsi ca nadīś caiva vanāni vividhāni ca atikramya sasādātha ramyāṃ dvāravatīṃ purīm
english: Crossing lakes and rivers and woodlands of many kinds, he then reached the lovely city of Dvāravatī.

sanskrit: vartamāne mahārāja mahe raivatakasya ca upāyāt puṇḍarīkākṣo yuyudhānānugas tadā
english: While the festival of Mount Raivataka was in progress, O great king, the lotus-eyed one approached, followed by Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: alaṃkṛtas tu sa girir nānārūpavicitritaiḥ babhau rukmamayaiḥ kāśaiḥ sarvataḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: That mountain, adorned and made wondrous with diverse forms, shone on every side with golden lattices, O bull among men.

sanskrit: kāñcanasragbhir agryābhiḥ sumanobhis tathaiva ca vāsobhiś ca mahāśailaḥ kalpavṛkṣaiś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: With choice golden garlands, with flowers, and with cloths, and with wish-granting trees on every side, was that great mountain bedecked.

sanskrit: dīpavṛkṣaiś ca sauvarṇair abhīkṣṇam upaśobhitaḥ guhānirjharadeśeṣu divābhūto babhūva ha
english: Resplendent throughout with golden lamp-trees, in the regions of its caves and cascades it became as bright as day.

sanskrit: patākābhir vicitrābhiḥ saghaṇṭābhiḥ samantataḥ puṃbhiḥ strībhiś ca saṃghuṣṭaḥ pragīta iva cābhavat atīva prekṣaṇīyo 'bhūn merur munigaṇair iva
english: With gay banners hung with bells on every side, resounding with the voices of men and women, it seemed to break into song; exceedingly fair to behold it was, like Meru thronged with hosts of sages.

sanskrit: mattānāṃ hṛṣṭarūpāṇāṃ strīṇāṃ puṃsāṃ ca bhārata gāyatāṃ parvatendrasya divaspṛg iva nisvanaḥ
english: The sound of women and men, flushed with drink and joyous in form, singing upon that lord of mountains, seemed, O Bhārata, to touch the very heavens.

sanskrit: pramattamattasaṃmattakṣveḍitotkṛṣṭasaṃkulā tathā kilakilāśabdair bhūr abhūt sumanoharā
english: Thronged with the shouts and roars of the heedless, the tipsy, and the wholly drunken, and with cries of merriment, the place became most enchanting.

sanskrit: vipaṇāpaṇavān ramyo bhakṣyabhojyavihāravān vastramālyotkarayuto vīṇāveṇumṛdaṅgavān
english: Lovely with its markets and stalls, rich in food to chew and food to eat and in pleasure-grounds, heaped with garments and garlands, and resounding with lute and flute and drum, it was.

sanskrit: surāmaireyamiśreṇa bhakṣyabhojyena caiva ha dīnāndhakṛpaṇādibhyo dīyamānena cāniśam babhau paramakalyāṇo mahas tasya mahāgireḥ
english: With wine and mead and with food to chew and to eat, given out without ceasing to the poor, the blind, the wretched, and the like, the most auspicious festival of that great mountain shone forth.

sanskrit: puṇyāvasathavān vīra puṇyakṛdbhir niṣevitaḥ vihāro vṛṣṇivīrāṇāṃ mahe raivatakasya ha sa nago veśmasaṃkīrṇo devaloka ivābabhau
english: Furnished with holy retreats, O hero, frequented by doers of holy deeds, the pleasure-ground of the Vṛṣṇi warriors at the festival of Raivataka — that mountain, crowded with dwellings, shone like the world of the gods.

sanskrit: tadā ca kṛṣṇasāṃnidhyam āsādya bharatarṣabha śakrasadmapratīkāśo babhūva sa hi śailarāṭ
english: And then, gaining the presence of Kṛṣṇa, O bull of the Bharatas, that king of mountains became the very likeness of the abode of Śakra.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpūjyamānaḥ sa viveśa bhavanaṃ śubham govindaḥ sātyakiś caiva jagāma bhavanaṃ svakam
english: Then Govinda, being honored, entered the splendid palace, while Sātyaki too went off to his own dwelling.

sanskrit: viveśa ca sa hṛṣṭātmā cirakālapravāsakaḥ kṛtvā nasukaraṃ karma dānaveṣv iva vāsavaḥ
english: Glad of heart, after a long sojourn abroad, he entered, having wrought a deed hard to accomplish, like Vāsava among the Dānavas.

sanskrit: upayātaṃ tu vārṣṇeyaṃ bhojavṛṣṇyandhakās tadā abhyagacchan mahātmānaṃ devā iva śatakratum
english: When the scion of the Vṛṣṇis had arrived, the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas then came forth to that great soul, as the gods come to the lord of a hundred sacrifices.

sanskrit: sa tān abhyarcya medhāvī pṛṣṭvā ca kuśalaṃ tadā abhyavādayata prītaḥ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ tathā
english: That wise one, having honored them and inquired after their welfare, then, well pleased, made his obeisance to his father and his mother.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ ca saṃpariṣvaktaḥ sāntvitaś ca mahābhujaḥ upopaviṣṭas taiḥ sarvair vṛṣṇibhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Embraced by the two of them and comforted, the mighty-armed one sat down, surrounded by all those Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: sa viśrānto mahātejāḥ kṛtapādāvasecanaḥ kathayām āsa taṃ kṛṣṇaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ pitrā mahāhavam
english: Then, rested, his feet bathed, that Kṛṣṇa of great splendor, when questioned by his father, recounted the great battle.

sanskrit: vasudeva uvāca śrutavān asmi vārṣṇeya saṃgrāmaṃ paramādbhutam narāṇāṃ vadatāṃ putra kathodghāteṣu nityaśaḥ
english: Vasudeva said: I have heard, O scion of the Vṛṣṇis, of that most marvelous battle, my son, continually, in the openings of men's tales as they spoke.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu pratyakṣadarśī ca kāryajñaś ca mahābhuja tasmāt prabrūhi saṃgrāmaṃ yāthātathyena me 'nagha
english: But you are one who saw it with your own eyes and who knows what was done, O mighty-armed one; therefore tell me the battle truly as it was, O sinless one.

sanskrit: yathā tad abhavad yuddhaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām bhīṣmakarṇakṛpadroṇaśalyādibhir anuttamam
english: How that unequaled war of the great-souled Pāṇḍavas was waged with Bhīṣma, Karṇa, Kṛpa, Droṇa, Śalya, and the rest —

sanskrit: anyeṣāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca kṛtāstrāṇām anekaśaḥ nānāveṣākṛtimatāṃ nānādeśanivāsinām
english: — and with many other warriors skilled in arms, of varied garb and form, dwellers in many lands.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ pitrā mātus tadantike śaśaṃsa kuruvīrāṇāṃ saṃgrāme nidhanaṃ yathā
english: Thus addressed by his father, the lotus-eyed one, in his mother's presence, related how the heroes of the Kurus had met their end in the battle.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca atyadbhutāni karmāṇi kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahātmanām bahulatvān na saṃkhyātuṃ śakyāny abdaśatair api
english: Vāsudeva said: The most wondrous deeds of those great-souled warriors, by reason of their multitude, could not be reckoned even in a hundred years.

sanskrit: prādhānyatas tu gadataḥ samāsenaiva me śṛṇu karmāṇi pṛthivīśānāṃ yathāvad amaradyute
english: But hear from me, as I tell it in brief and by its chief points, the deeds of those lords of the earth, faithfully, O you of godlike radiance.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaḥ senāpatir abhūd ekādaśacamūpatiḥ kauravyaḥ kauraveyāṇāṃ devānām iva vāsavaḥ
english: Bhīṣma the Kuru was the commander of the Kauravas, lord of eleven armies, as Vāsava is over the gods.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ netā saptacamūpatiḥ babhūva rakṣito dhīmān dhīmatā savyasācinā
english: Śikhaṇḍin was the leader of the sons of Pāṇḍu, lord of seven armies; the wise one was guarded by the wise Savyasācin.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad abhavad yuddhaṃ daśāhāni mahātmanām kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca sumahad romaharṣaṇam
english: For ten days raged that battle of those great souls, the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, vast and hair-raising.

sanskrit: tataḥ śikhaṇḍī gāṅgeyam ayudhyantaṃ mahāhave jaghāna bahubhir bāṇaiḥ saha gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: Then Śikhaṇḍin, together with the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, struck down with many arrows the son of Gaṅgā as he refused to fight in that great battle.

sanskrit: akarot sa tataḥ kālaṃ śaratalpagato muniḥ ayanaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ hitvā saṃprāpte cottarāyaṇe
english: Then that sage, lying upon his bed of arrows, made his end, forsaking the southern course of the sun and awaiting the coming of the northern.

sanskrit: tataḥ senāpatir abhūd droṇo 'straviduṣāṃ varaḥ pravīraḥ kauravendrasya kāvyo daityapater iva
english: Then Droṇa, the best of those versed in weapons, became commander, the great hero of the Kaurava lord, as Kāvya was of the king of the Daityas.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇībhiḥ śiṣṭābhir navabhir dvijasattamaḥ saṃvṛtaḥ samaraślāghī guptaḥ kṛpavṛṣādibhiḥ
english: That best of the twice-born, glorying in battle, was surrounded by the nine armies that remained, and guarded by Kṛpa, the Bull, and the others.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tv abhūn netā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahāstravit gupto bhīmena tejasvī mitreṇa varuṇo yathā
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna, great knower of weapons, became the leader of the Pāṇḍavas, that splendid one guarded by Bhīma as Varuṇa is by his ally.

sanskrit: pañcasenāparivṛto droṇaprepsur mahāmanāḥ pitur nikārān saṃsmṛtya raṇe karmākaron mahat
english: Surrounded by five hosts, that high-minded one, eager to come at Droṇa, remembering the insults done to his father, performed a great feat in the fray.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs te pṛthivīpālā droṇapārṣatasaṃgare nānādigāgatā vīrāḥ prāyaśo nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: In that encounter between Droṇa and the son of Pṛṣata, those lords of the earth, heroes come from many quarters, for the most part met their death.

sanskrit: dināni pañca tad yuddham abhūt paramadāruṇam tato droṇaḥ pariśrānto dhṛṣṭadyumnavaśaṃ gataḥ
english: For five days that battle raged, most terrible; then Droṇa, worn out, fell into the power of Dhṛṣṭadyumna.
